info.name: Moderation Service
info.description: Moderation Service through the Gateway. Set base_url to the Gateway (http://localhost:8080) and service_token to the stack's SERVICE_TOKEN; every request carries the service prefix /api/v1/moderation. The scenarios use the built-in mocks (SESSION_URL, APPLICANT_URL, CREDENTIAL_URL, UNIVERSITY_RECORD_URL and RULES_URL empty, DEV_ENDPOINTS=true). Run the folders in order; the Setup folder resets the session so the run can be repeated.

variable.description: The Gateway. Every request below carries the service prefix /api/v1/moderation
JWT_SECRET of the Gateway in the stack's .env; the pre-request script signs the player token with it
The stack's SERVICE_TOKEN (.env of the team compose); the Gateway checks it on /admin/* and /dev/*
The Moderator of the mock session. Sent as X-Player-Id, the header the Gateway sets after validating the player's JWT
The service's MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS; the 429 demo fires this many slow requests first

item.name: reset: delete this session's decisions and bans (admin)

header.description: Set by the Gateway in the real flow; sent here because the Gateway auth part is not merged yet, and a client value is discarded once it is

request.description: Decisions are immutable, so a second run of this collection would get 409 ALREADY_DECIDED. This request lists the session's decisions and deletes them, plus the ban list entries they created, through the admin endpoints, so the collection can be run again and again.

exec: // GET /bans is a player route: the Gateway wants a JWT, not X-Player-Id. pm.sendRequest skips the
// collection pre-request script, so the token is signed here the same way.
const unsigned = part({ alg: 'HS256', typ: 'JWT' }) + '.' + part({ sub: pm.variables.get('moderator_id'), iat: now, exp: now + 300 });
const playerHeaders = [{ key: 'Authorization', value: 'Bearer ' + unsigned + '.' + b64url(cryptoJs.HmacSHA256(unsigned, pm.variables.get('jwt_secret'))) }];
console.log('reset: deleting ' + items.length + ' decision(s) of session ' + sid);

items.forEach(d => pm.sendRequest({ url: base + '/api/v1/moderation/admin/decisions/' + d.decision_id, method: 'DELETE', header: svcHeaders }, (err, res) => console.log('delete decision', d.decision_id.slice(0, 8), err ? String(err) : res.code)));
pm.sendRequest({ url: base + '/api/v1/moderation/bans?q=FAF23104&limit=100', method: 'GET', header: playerHeaders }, (err, res) => {
if (err || !res) { console.log('ban lookup failed', String(err)); return; }

(res.json().items || []).filter(b => b.session_id === sid).forEach(b => pm.sendRequest({ url: base + '/api/v1/moderation/admin/bans/' + b.ban_id, method: 'DELETE', header: svcHeaders }, (e, r) => console.log('delete ban', b.ban_id.slice(0, 8), e ? String(e) : r.code)));

item.name: GET /admin/events (outbox with the delivery state per consumer, oldest first)

request.description: Every decision.recorded event with its envelope and the delivery state per consumer: the relay pushes it to Server Moderation Session Service's POST /api/v1/events through the Gateway (2xx = delivered, 422 = parked, anything else retried with backoff).

exec: pm.test('one delivery per consumer, addressed to session', () => { pm.expect(e.deliveries).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(e.deliveries[0].consumer).to.eql('session'); pm.expect(['pending', 'delivered']).to.include(e.deliveries[0].status); });

item.name: GET /dev/mock/events (the relay delivered decision.recorded to the mock Session)

exec: // The relay pushes the outbox every RELAY_INTERVAL (1 s by default); give it a moment.
pm.test('the mock Session accepted the events of this run', () => pm.expect(body.total).to.be.at.least(1));
pm.test('the last one is the first-year decision', () => pm.expect(body.items[body.items.length - 1].payload.decision_id).to.eql(pm.variables.get('last_decision_id')));

item.name: 6. Task timeout and concurrent task limit
GET /dev/slow?ms=7000 is stopped by the task timeout: 408 REQUEST_TIMEOUT

exec: pm.test('REQUEST_TIMEOUT with the timeout in details', () => { const e = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(e.code).to.eql('REQUEST_TIMEOUT'); pm.expect(e.details.timeout_ms).to.be.a('number'); });
pm.test('answered at the service timeout (5 s), not after 7 s', () => pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(6500));

request.description: The Gateway allows 10 s, the service 5 s: the service gives up first and the Gateway passes its 408 through unchanged.

item.name: the request above MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS is refused at once: 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS

exec: // Fill every slot with slow tasks, then send the request above the limit and keep its answer for the tests.
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) pm.sendRequest({ url: slow, method: 'GET', header: headers }, () => {});
// A moment for the burst to reach the service, then the one request too many.
pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.variables.get('base_url') + '/api/v1/moderation/dev/slow?ms=100', method: 'GET', header: headers }, (err, res) => {
let body = null; try { body = res.json(); } catch (e) {}
pm.variables.set('overflow', JSON.stringify({ error: err ? String(err) : null, status: res && res.code, retryAfter: res && res.headers.get('Retry-After'), body, ms: Date.now() - started }));
pm.test('the request above the limit got 429', () => { pm.expect(overflow.error, 'request error').to.eql(null); pm.expect(overflow.status).to.eql(429); });
pm.test('liveness stays exempt while the service is full', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: The whole check runs from the scripts, because a script waits for its own pm.sendRequest calls before the request itself is sent: the pre-request fills every slot with slow tasks, sends one more shortly after and keeps its answer; the tests check that answer. The request of this item is only the liveness check, which stays exempt while the service is full.

item.name: after the burst the service accepts work again

exec: // Through the Gateway a player is identified by a JWT (HS256, JWT_SECRET shared with Player Service),
// never by X-Player-Id: the Gateway checks the token, discards any client-sent X-Player-Id and sets
// its own from the token's sub. Rather than logging in through Player Service, this script signs
// the token itself: every request that names a player in X-Player-Id gets
// Authorization: Bearer <jwt> with sub = that id, and the X-Player-Id header is dropped.
// jwt_secret must equal JWT_SECRET of the Gateway in the stack's .env.
const unsigned = part({ alg: 'HS256', typ: 'JWT' }) + '.' + part({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 300 });
